info.title: VenueRelay Event Operations API
info.description: Node.js API for HS-0130. Operational commands atomically commit state, immutable history and durable in-app notifications. Use authenticated event WebSockets for invalidations and role-filtered snapshots for records. Dates use ISO 8601 UTC.

post.description: Creates a staff username/password account and session without email. Provide username (3–30 ASCII characters); legacy clients may instead provide email. Usernames are normalised to lowercase and unique. Username accounts always receive immediate access and a private recovery code. No attendee signup is needed for public QR requests. Legacy email behavior: With EMAIL_TRANSPORT=disabled (default), accessGranted is true immediately, emailVerified remains false, and a private recoveryCode is returned once. Save it securely; it is stored hashed. With an email transport, DNS validation and single-use email verification apply. API clients set X-Rally-Client: api to receive sessionToken. Do not automatically retry signup.

post.summary: Reset password using a private recovery code
post.description: Rate limited by account and IP. Atomically replaces the password and single-use recovery code, cancels pending resets and revokes sessions. MongoDB also removes device push subscriptions. Returns a replacement recoveryCode once; save it before signing in. Invalid or replayed codes return 401 without changing records. Keep the code secret. Do not automatically retry: if the response is lost, sign in with the new password.

post.summary: Issue a single-use WebSocket ticket (MongoDB hosting)
post.description: Browser session required; integration tokens denied. POST through the website origin, then connect to the Render wss endpoint /api/v1/events/{eventId}/live?ticket=VALUE within 30 seconds. The ticket is event-, origin- and role-bound and consumed once. Fetch a fresh ticket on every reconnect. Never put session tokens in URLs. Local SQLite connects with its same-origin cookie instead.

post.description: Stable key required per intent. Reuse it after a timeout, retry, crash or reconnect. Keys are unique per actor, retained indefinitely. Replay returns original entity with replayed=true. Same key with different payload: 409 IDEMPOTENCY_MISMATCH. Task updates require expectedVersion; stale writes: 409 VERSION_CONFLICT with details.current. Permissions, transaction, immutable history and notifications apply to every command. Only organisers assign and verify closure. See docs/API.md for transitions and payloads.

get.description: Connect with ws/wss and an allowed Origin. Local same-origin connections use the session cookie. Hosted MongoDB connections use a fresh one-use ticket from POST /events/{eventId}/live-ticket in the ticket query parameter. Optional local persona query and ticket personas are restricted to the owning demo account. Receives connected and event.changed messages containing only eventId. On invalidation refetch the role-filtered snapshot. Reconnect with backoff; polling is a fallback. Auth is rechecked on heartbeat and account changes; session revocation closes with 4401. Commands always use HTTP with idempotency keys.

post.description: Persist a random 32-byte base64url receiptKey and stable request key on the device BEFORE sending. Reuse both and the identical body after timeout/reload/reconnect. A new key is a new request. Transaction atomically creates a lightweight attendee reporter, one task, command, audit, notifications and hashed receipt; no user account or password hashing. Same key with changed body/link:409. Return does not contain receiptKey. Open /request#key=RECEIPT_KEY. 120 attempts/minute per event and 60/minute per server peer. Respect Retry-After; no unbounded retries. Names are self-reported, not verified. Public input cannot assign owners or change task status.

get.summary: Read exactly one request using its private receipt
get.description: Authorization: Bearer vr_guest_RECEIPT_KEY. Only its event metadata, request and status history; no member list, account data, raw audit snapshots or unrelated requests. No write access. The browser refreshes every 15 seconds while visible. Anyone holding the link can read it; keep it private. Missing/unknown receipts:404. Receipt remains valid when the public event link is disabled. Tokens remain in URL fragments, not query strings or server access-log paths.
